newsitem.title: USA: Chrysler debuts new Jeep, brings back "300" name.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler debuts new Jeep, brings back "300" name.

text.p: Chrysler Corp., seeking new flagship vehicles, said Wednesday it will bring back its "300" nameplate on a sports sedan next year and will debut a new ultra-luxury version of its Jeep Grand Cherokee powered by a monster V-8 engine.

Introduced at the New York Auto Show, the Grand Cherokee 5.9 Limited will be the fastest Jeep ever, equipped with the biggest engine available in a sport utility vehicle -- a 245-horsepower, 5.9-liter V-8 engine.
It also will be loaded with luxury features, including seats and interior parts swathed in calf leather and maple woodgrain trim.
Pricing has not yet been announced, but it is expected to be above the current Grand Cherokee, which tops out in the low- to mid-$30,000 range.

It will compete with a slew of new luxury sport utility vehicles coming in the next year from Mercedes-Benz AG, Toyota Motor Corp.'s Lexus Division, Nissan Motor Co. Ltd.'s Infiniti Division and others.

Production of the 1998 model year Grand Cherokee 5.9 Limited begins in the fall at Chrysler's Jefferson North Assembly Plant in Detroit. The vehicle will also be assembled in Graz, Austria and sold in overseas markets as the 1998 Grand Cherokee LX.
The vehicle's exterior features a modified grille, a louvered hood and standard sunroof.

"The 5.9 Limited offers our customers a vehicle that is unique to the Jeep brand and the sport utility segment," said Martin Levine, General Manager of the Chrysler Plymouth Jeep Eagle Division. "The more powerful V-8 engine, added luxury features and Jeep capability positions the Grand Cherokee 5.9 Limited as our flagship vehicle for the Jeep brand.
Levine said production volume for the 5.9 Limited will depend on market demand. Chrysler sold 279,195 Jeep Grand Cherokees in 1996.
"They say we have the flexibility to meet free market demand," he added.

Chrysler also said it will use the 300M name on an all-new Chrysler-brand sports sedan to be introduced next year. The new car, based on Chrysler's new-generation "LH" large car platform, will be launched in the spring of 1998 and is aimed at strengthening Chrysler's premium brand image.
The 300 nameplate was used on Chrysler's top-of-the-line cars in the 1950s and 1960s, which featured powerful engines combined with roominess and graceful styling.
